name: Rhea from Voyager 1, November 12, 1980
blurb: Saturn's moon Rhea, about 1,530 kilometers across. Seen by Voyager 1's narrow-angle camera through orange, green and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Rhea, fully lit, from about 1.3 million kilometers away, 14 hours before Voyager 1's closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980. Saturn's second largest moon is made largely of water ice and is more heavily cratered than Dione and Tethys.
